paper.title: Information-Theoretic Regret Bounds for Bandits with Fixed Expert Advice

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with fixed (known) expert advice / policy set Theta
unmapped: experts are fixed, known distributions over the K actions (policy set Theta of N policies, constant over time)
the learner knows the policy set Theta
learner picks a policy, action sampled from it; observes the action and its loss
each arm is in the support of at least one policy
settings.definition_quote: We consider a non-stochastic multi-armed bandits problem with a finite action set $\mathcal{A} = [K]$ containing $K$ actions, and a (fixed) policy set $\Theta \in \Delta_{K-1}$ consisting of $N$ probability distributions over the actions. ... the decision maker selects a policy $\theta_t \in \Theta$; an action $A_t \in [K]$ is then sampled from $\theta_t$; the decision maker subsequently suffers the loss $\ell_t(A_t)$ and observes the pair $\big(A_t,\ell_t(A_t)\big)$.

algorithms.name: OSMD on the Convex Hull of Policies

symbols.S_star: S^*(Theta) = sum_j (max_theta theta(j) - min_theta theta(j)), similarity index of the policy set

source.label: upper:alt-losses:thm
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{exp4} run with $\eta = \sqrt{ \frac{2\log N}{T \mathcal{S}^*(\Theta)}}$ satisfies $R_T \leq \sqrt{2 T \mathcal{S}^*(\Theta) \log N}.$

results.notes: Regret against best fixed policy in hindsight, expectation over internal randomization. Tuning requires knowing Theta (hence S*) and T.

symbols.D_star: D^*(Theta) = min_tau max_theta KL(theta, tau), KL width of the policy set (<= log N)

source.label: cvxhull-thm
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{osmd} run with $\tau^* \in \argmin_{\tau\in\Delta_{K-1}} D(\Theta||\tau)$ and $\eta=\sqrt{ \frac{2D^*(\Theta)}{T K}}$ satisfies $R_T \leq \sqrt{2TD^*(\Theta)K}$.

results.notes: Requires projection onto co(Theta); computational complexity not discussed.

symbols.M_supp: support size of each uniform policy
symbols.V_common: number of arms common to all policies

conditions: Theta is the radially symmetric uniform policy structure of Example 2 (uniform policies over M arms, pairwise support intersections identical)

source.label: low:flower:thm
source.quote: If $\Theta$ conforms to the structure of Example \ref{example-flower} such that $M > V$. Then for any algorithm and $T \geq \frac{N M}{4 \log(4/3)(M-V)}$, there exists a sequence of losses such that $R_T \geq \frac{1}{18} \sqrt{N\frac{M-V}{M} T}.$

results.notes: Equals sqrt(S^*(Theta) T)/18 in this case; matches Theorem 1 up to log factor. Proof via stochastic Bernoulli losses.

symbols.eps_unif: mixing parameter epsilon in [0,1] of the epsilon-uniform policy structure

conditions: Theta is the epsilon-uniform structure of Example 4 (N = K, theta(j) = (1-eps)/K + eps*I{j = a_theta})

source.label: thm:eps-uniform
source.quote: If $\Theta$ conforms to the $\epsilon$-uniform structure of Example \ref{example-epsilon}. Then for $T \geq \frac{K}{4\log(4/3)}$ and any algorithm, there exists a sequence of losses such that $R_T \geq \frac{1}{18}\epsilon\sqrt{KT}.$

symbols.H2: squared Hellinger distance between the two policies

source.label: thm:H2
source.quote: Assume that $\Theta=\{\theta_1,\theta_2\}$ and $H^2(\theta_1,\theta_2) > 0$. Then for any algorithm and $T \geq \frac{1}{8\log(4/3)H^2(\theta_1,\theta_2)}$, there exists a sequence of losses such that $R_T \geq \frac{1}{13}\sqrt{H^2(\theta_1,\theta_2)T}.$

conditions: exists a policy set (multi-task structure) with K >= 2, S^*(Theta) = q for any integer q >= 2, and S^*(Theta) log N = K D^*(Theta)

source.label: th:worst-case-lower
source.quote: For any integer $q\geq2$, there exists a problem structure where $K\geq2$, $\mathcal{S}^*(\Theta) = q$, and $\mathcal{S}^*(\Theta) \log N = K D^*(\Theta)$; such that any algorithm, for sufficiently large $T$, suffers $\Omega\left(\sqrt{\mathcal{S}^*(\Theta) T \frac{\log N}{\log \mathcal{S}^*(\Theta)}}\right)$ regret.

results.notes: Existential lower bound for a specific policy-set construction; follows from Theorem 8.

conditions: policy set has the multi-task structure: K = qM arms in M sections of q >= 2 arms, Theta = all uniform policies over M arms with one arm per section (N = q^M)

source.label: low:multi:thm
source.quote: Suppose that the policy and arm spaces conform to the multi-task structure. Then for any algorithm and $T \geq \frac{K}{4\log(4/3)}$, there exists a sequence of losses such that \begin{equation*} R_T \geq \frac{1}{18} \sqrt{K T}. \end{equation*}
